title: Bulb Planting
strapline: Tuck the papery bulb into the cold autumn soil, pat it in, and wait all winter for the surprise that comes up in spring.
intent: Planting bulbs in autumn for a spring that feels impossibly far away teaches children the deepest kind of patience — a reward that arrives months later, when they have half forgotten.
Choosing which way is up, digging the right-sized hole and settling each bulb builds fine-motor control and thoughtful, careful work.
Children learn that a dry, dead-looking bulb holds a living plant, and that soil, water, cold and time will wake it — real knowledge of how growing things work.
The long wait connects children to the seasons — planting as the year closes down, watching for shoots as it wakes back up.
Digging, spacing, counting and comparing bulbs weaves mathematics into a real job with a real purpose.
Growing vocabulary takes root — bulb, shoot, root, soil, sprout, bloom, spring, patience.
implementation: Plant in autumn with real tools — trowels, bulbs (daffodils, crocus, tulips), pots and beds — and let children do the digging, placing and covering themselves.
Talk through the puzzle as you go: 'Which way up do you think it goes? It looks dead, but there's a whole flower asleep inside.'
Space and count the bulbs together — three in this pot, a row along the bed — bringing in number and spacing as part of the job.
Mark and label where you planted, then let the waiting begin, revisiting the spot through the winter to check.
When the first green shoots come, celebrate loudly and photograph the change from bare soil to bloom.
Send a planted pot home with each child so the wonder of the spring surprise reaches families too.
key_questions: Which way up do you think it goes? It looks dead — but what might be asleep inside?
How many bulbs shall we plant in this pot?
What do you think this bulb needs to wake up?
How far apart should we space them along the bed?
What do you think we'll see here in the spring?

playing_exploring: Children dig, handle and plant real bulbs in real soil, following the whole hands-on job from start to finish.
They explore the puzzle of a dry bulb that hides a living flower.
active_learning: Children wait months for their bulbs to appear and keep checking the spot, learning that some rewards take a long time and are worth it.
creating_thinking: Children reason about which way up the bulb goes and what it needs, and link the cold soil and passing seasons to the flower that finally comes up.
